picks.editorial_note: Published in Nature, this work shows AI can autonomously propose novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups — a rare case of AI advancing the scientific method itself rather than just accelerating existing workflows.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: An international team's Nature-published HydroGym platform trains physics-informed RL agents to actively control fluid dynamics, with direct applications spanning energy, transportation, and defense systems.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's GSCo framework pairs a generalist medical AI with lightweight specialist models, a scalable architecture pattern for precision healthcare that also reflects strong cross-institutional collaboration.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: A $30 million NSF Science and Technology Center, led by Michigan State with Georgia Tech and others, represents a major sustained federal investment in predictive modeling for turbulence — foundational science with energy and aerospace payoffs.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: EPFL's framework for training LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty tackles a core reliability problem in AI-driven science, potentially making automated experimental design trustworthy enough for real lab use.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's nationwide German permit for its Level 4 autonomous research vehicle marks a concrete regulatory milestone for open-source autonomous driving platforms, signaling growing government confidence in AI-driven mobility.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Federal cancellation of AHRQ healthcare research grants, including a Johns Hopkins AI project on lung cancer diagnosis timelines, illustrates how funding policy shifts are directly disrupting applied AI research with patient-safety implications.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient

picks.editorial_note: A $2.88 million DOE award to a University of Houston-led coalition targets AI-driven discovery of critical-mineral-free magnets, tying AI research directly to U.S. supply chain security policy.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: A pointed viewpoint from Helmholtz researchers arguing Germany and Europe must build sovereign open frontier AI models reflects a growing policy debate over AI dependence on U.S. and Chinese models.
picks.title: Why we in Germany and Europe need to build our own open frontier models

picks.editorial_note: A $1.2 million NSF grant spanning USF, Purdue, and UT Dallas addresses quantum-resistant, AI-enabled security for next-generation wireless networks, pairing near-term funding with long-horizon infrastructure security relevance.
picks.title: USF faculty secure $1.2M NSF grant to advance quantum-secure, AI-enabled wireless networks
